speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are an 8-month-old boy having trouble feeding and feeling full in your tummy. To help me understand what is wrong, can you tell me if your vomit ever looks like it has white, curd-like specks in it?

speaker: Patient
text: The baby has been very fussy, feeding less than usual, and the abdomen looks distended. Crying gets worse when the belly is touched.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Pyloric Stenosis

*Note: While the initial question about "curd-like specks" (suggesting GERD) was asked, the clinical picture of an 8-month-old with worsening fussiness, feeding difficulties, abdominal distension, and significant tenderness (crying on touch) strongly points towards an obstruction like Intussusception or Pyloric Stenosis. Given the age (8 months) where pyloric stenosis is less common than in infants 3-6 weeks, Intussusception is a primary differential. However, the specific finding of a distended, tender abdomen is critical. I will proceed with the diagnosis based on the most acute presentation.*
